arxiv-2208-01389.title: Measurement of charged-particle jet properties in p–Pb collisions at s NN = 5.02 \sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02 TeV with ALICE
arxiv-2208-01389.creator: Prottoy Das on behalf of ALICE Collaboration
arxiv-2208-01389.description: Abstract We present the measurement of charged-particle jet properties in minimum bias p–Pb collisions at s NN \sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02 TeV in ALICE. Jets are reconstructed from charged particles at midrapidity using the anti- k T k_{\rm T} jet finding algorithm with jet resolution parameter R R = 0.4.

arxiv-2212-04440.title: Nikola Tesla’s Inventions - Myth or Reality?
arxiv-2212-04440.creator: Val G. Rousseau, https://vadcpa.com/Val
arxiv-2212-04440.description: Abstract Nikola Tesla is often presented by his adepts as the “unjustly forgotten genius”, without who our current technology wouldn’t exist. In this paper, we analyze some popular statements made by Tesla’s adepts, mostly about inventions that they attribute to him, and determine whether they are myth or reality. arxiv-2302-11668.title: Graphs with minimum fractional domatic number
arxiv-2302-11668.creator: Maximilien Gadouleau, Nathaniel Harms, George B. Mertzios, Viktor Zamaraev
arxiv-2302-11668.description: Abstract The domatic number of a graph is the maximum number of vertex disjoint dominating sets that partition the vertex set of the graph. In this paper we consider the fractional variant of this notion. Graphs with fractional domatic number 1 are exactly the graphs that contain an isolated vertex.

arxiv-2403-08912.title: Current experimental upper bounds on spacetime diffusion
arxiv-2403-08912.creator: Martijn Janse, Dennis G. Uitenbroek, Loek van Everdingen, Jaimy Plugge, Bas Hensen, Tjerk H. Oosterkamp
arxiv-2403-08912.description: Abstract A consistent theory describing the dynamics of quantum systems interacting on a classical spacetime was recently put forward by Oppenheim et al..[1, 2]. Quantum states may retain their coherence, at the cost of some amount of stochasticity of the spacetime metric, characterized by a spacetime diffusion parameter.

arxiv-2407-06020.title: Electron-only magnetic reconnection and inverse magnetic-energy transfer at sub-ion scales
arxiv-2407-06020.creator: Zhuo Liu, Caio Silva, Lucio M. Milanese, Muni Zhou, Noah R. Mandell, Nuno F. Loureiro
arxiv-2407-06020.description: Abstract We derive, and validate numerically, an analytical model for electron-only magnetic reconnection applicable to strongly magnetized plasmas. Our model predicts sub-ion-scale reconnection rates significantly higher than those pertaining to large-scale reconnection, aligning with recent observations and simulations. We apply this reconnection model to the problem of inverse magnetic energy transfer at sub-ion scales.

arxiv-2501-09567.title: Bridging conformal field theory and parton approaches to SU ​ ( n ) k \mathrm{SU}(n)_{k} chiral spin liquids
arxiv-2501-09567.creator: Tong Liu, Ying-Hai Wu, Hong-Hao Tu, Tao Xiang
arxiv-2501-09567.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tong Liu, Ying-Hai Wu, Hong-Hao Tu, Tao Xiang. We employ the SU ​ ( n ) k \mathrm{SU}(n)_{k} Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model in conformal field theory to construct lattice wave functions in both one and two dimensions. The spins on all lattice sites are chosen to transform under the SU ⁡ ( n ) \mathrm{SU}(n) irreducible representation with a single row and k k boxes in the Young tableau.

arxiv-2504-03292.title: FaR: Enhancing Multi-Concept Text-to-Image Diffusion via Concept Fusion and Localized Refinement
arxiv-2504-03292.creator: Gia-Nghia Tran, Quang-Huy Che, Trong-Tai Dam Vu, Bich-Nga Pham, Vinh-Tiep Nguyen, Trung-Nghia Le, Minh-Triet Tran
arxiv-2504-03292.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gia-Nghia Tran, Quang-Huy Che, Trong-Tai Dam Vu, Bich-Nga Pham, Vinh-Tiep Nguyen, Trung-Nghia Le, Minh-Triet Tran. Generating multiple new concepts remains a challenging problem in the text-to-image task. Current methods often overfit when trained on a small number of samples and struggle with attribute leakage, particularly for class-similar subjects (e.g., two specific dogs). In this paper, we introduce Fuse-and-Refine (FaR), a novel approach that tackles these challenges through two key contributions: Concept Fusion technique and Localized Refinement loss function.

arxiv-2505-13533.title: FinMaster: A Holistic Benchmark for Mastering Full-Pipeline Financial Workflows with LLMs
arxiv-2505-13533.creator: Junzhe Jiang, Chang Yang, Aixin Cui, Sihan Jin, Ruiyu Wang, Bo Li, Xiao Huang, Dongning Sun, Xinrun Wang
arxiv-2505-13533.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Junzhe Jiang, Chang Yang, Aixin Cui, Sihan Jin, Ruiyu Wang, Bo Li, Xiao Huang, Dongning Sun, Xinrun Wang. Financial tasks are pivotal to global economic stability; however, their efficient execution faces persistent challenges, including labor intensive processes, low error tolerance, data fragmentation, and limitations in existing technological tools.

arxiv-2510-22849.title: Once Upon an Input: Reasoning via Per-Instance Program Synthesis
arxiv-2510-22849.creator: Adam Stein, Neelay Velingker, Mayur Naik, Eric Wong
arxiv-2510-22849.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) excel at zero-shot inference but continue to struggle with complex, multi-step reasoning. Recent methods that augment LLMs with intermediate reasoning steps such as Chain of Thought (CoT) and Program of Thought (PoT) improve performance but often produce undesirable solutions, especially in algorithmic domains.

arxiv-2512-17708.title: Review of MEMS Speakers for Audio Applications
arxiv-2512-17708.creator: Nils Wittek, Anton Melnikov, Bert Kaiser, André Zimmermann
arxiv-2512-17708.description: Abstract Microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) speakers are compact, scalable alternatives to traditional voice coil speakers, promising improved sound quality through precise semiconductor manufacturing. This review provides an overview of the research landscape, including ultrasound pulse-based and thermoacoustic sound generation, classifying MEMS speakers by actuation principle: electrodynamic, piezoelectric, and electrostatic.

arxiv-2601-10496.title: Model See, Model Do? Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Bug-vs-Fix Preference in Code LLMs CCS: Software and its engineering Software verification and validation CCS: Computing methodologies Natural language processing
arxiv-2601-10496.creator: Ali Al-Kaswan, Claudio Spiess, Prem Devanbu, Arie van Deursen, Maliheh Izadi
arxiv-2601-10496.description: Abstract . Large language models are increasingly used for code generation and debugging, but their outputs can still contain bugs that originate from training data. Distinguishing whether an LLM prefers correct code, or a familiar incorrect version might be influenced by what it’s been exposed to during training.

hartmann-principles-of-astrological-geom.description: Hartmann's geomancy manual after Agrippa — the 19th-century revival of the divinatory art.

pmc-11642103.title: Identifying Demographic and Clinical Determinants of Ischemic Workup in Patients with Heart Failure
pmc-11642103.creator: Kristen M John, Peter Wenn, Ofek Hai, Roman Zeltser, Amgad N Makaryus, Gani Bajraktari
pmc-11642103.description: Background/Objectives: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a common and treatable cause of heart failure (HF), but ischemic evaluation is often overlooked when evaluating patients with new-onset HF. Here, we sought to discern demographic and clinical predictors of ischemic workup in patients with newly diagnosed HF.

pmc-12389748.title: The Influence of Ultra-Wideband Anchor Placement on Localization Accuracy
pmc-12389748.creator: Luka Kramarić, Mario Muštra, Tomislav Radišić
pmc-12389748.description: Localization of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in spaces with a limited availability of Global Navigation Satellite System signals presents a challenge, and one possible solution is the usage of Ultra-Wideband (UWB) transceivers as an aid in the localization process. This paper examines the influence of placing the UWB anchors on the UAVs’ localization accuracy in indoor spaces.

pmc-12672781.title: A case of diabetic foot with severe vascular disease in an elderly no-option patient undergoing lower limb arterialization: a clinical case report
pmc-12672781.creator: Adriano Massacesi, Gioia Palmonella, Cristina Gatti, Michela Fichetti, Enrico Paci
pmc-12672781.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This clinical case report describes an 80-year-old no-option diabetic patient with chronic limb-threatening ischemia and severe vascular disease. The patient presented with wet gangrene and underwent an unsuccessful revascularization attempt, followed by minor amputation complicated by poor wound healing. Due to persistent ischemia and surgical dehiscence, the patient underwent a transcatheter deep venous arterialization procedure, resulting in improved perfusion, wound healing, and limb salvage.

pmc-12708817.title: Garden classification of femoral neck fracture using deep-learning algorithm
pmc-12708817.creator: Jaebeom Yang, Jinyong Park, Keunwoo Park, Eic Ju Lim, Ji Wan Kim, Jihoon Kweon, Chul-Ho Kim
pmc-12708817.description: The Garden classification, based on X-ray interpretation and established over 50 years ago, remains the standard clinical classification system for femoral neck fractures (FNFs). Yet, this classification has a high interobserver variability of 70%. We sought to develop a deep-learning algorithm capable of accurately predicting FNF types, using only X-ray images, with performance comparable to that of computed tomography (CT).

pmc-13375683.title: Oral Microbial Extracellular Vesicles as Novel Mediators of Alzheimer’s Pathogenesis: A Critical Review of the Periodontal–Brain Axis
pmc-13375683.creator: Seyed Ebrahim Alavi, Hasan Ebrahimi Shahmabadi, Robert M Love, Arun V Kurumathur, Lavanya A Sharma, Ajay Sharma
pmc-13375683.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder whose origins extend beyond the brain. Chronic periodontitis has emerged as a modifiable risk factor, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) have recently been proposed as important mediators of the periodontal–brain axis. Periodontal pathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis) release bacterial EVs enriched with virulence factors including gingipains, lipopolysaccharide, and regulatory RNAs.

uslaw-usc-t48-s1502.description: United States Code, Title 48 (Territories And Insular Possessions); Chapter 11 (Alien Owners Of Land). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. This chapter shall not apply to land owned in any of the Territories of the United States by aliens, which was acquired on or before March 3, 1887, so long as it is held by the then owners, their heirs or legal.
